quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When you tailgate other drivers (drive too close to their rear bumper), what happens?

options.text: You can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
You cannot get a traffic citation.
You help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Most rear-end collisions happen because of tailgating. To avoid tailgating, use the Three Second Rule. When the car ahead passes a point like a sign, count to three. If you reach that point before you finish counting, you are too close.

questions.question: A traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's directions. This is true even if the officer's directions go against traffic laws, signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: After a traffic collision, when must you file a written report with the DMV?

options.text: Only if someone is injured.
If property damage is over $1,000 or if anyone is injured.
Only if you are at fault.

questions.correctAnswerText: If property damage is over $1,000 or if anyone is injured.
questions.explanation: You must file a report with the DMV within 10 days if the collision caused a death, any injury, or more than $1,000 in property damage. Your insurance agent or lawyer can file the report for you.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. What should you do to prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to ride on water and lose grip with the road. This makes it hard to control your car.

questions.question: You are about to turn left at a corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming cars also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a Walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay close to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
Passing on the right is allowed when it is safe.
Passing on the left is allowed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross the center line to pass if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, when can you go?

options.text: When you come to a complete stop first.
When the light changes.
When you are in the right lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the right lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can proceed in that direction when the road is clear. This works whether the arrow is shown alone or with another signal.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Everyone can pass.
Only the side with the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is dashed, only traffic next to the dashed line can cross to pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: Is it ever okay to block an intersection during rush hour?

options.text: Yes, if your light is green.
No, never, even if your light is green.
Yes, if you have the right-of-way or a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never, even if your light is green.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. You can get a ticket for blocking the intersection.

questions.question: You see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm out. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has its lights flashing and arm extended. Stay stopped until the arm goes back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or opposite.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with no curb, which way should your front wheels point?

options.text: Left, toward the street.
Right, away from the street.
Straight, parallel with the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, away from the street.
questions.explanation: On a hill with no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the road if the brakes fail. Do this whether parking uphill or downhill.

questions.question: You drive 55 mph in a 55 mph zone. Can you get a speeding ticket?

options.text: No, it is always legal.
Yes, if road or weather conditions require a slower speed.
Yes, only if you are near a sharp curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if road or weather conditions require a slower speed.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even if the posted speed limit is higher. Consider the speed of other cars, road surface, bicyclists, pedestrians, and weather when deciding your speed.

questions.question: When making a right turn at a corner where there is a bicycle lane, what must you do?

options.text: You cannot enter the bicycle lane.
You should only enter the bicycle lane if you stop first.
You must enter the bicycle lane before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must enter the bicycle lane before turning.
questions.explanation: You must move into the bicycle lane no more than 200 feet before the corner and then turn. Make sure no bicyclists are in your way before moving.

questions.question: Which child needs a child passenger restraint system?

options.text: A 9-year-old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall
A 10-year-old who is 5 feet 3 inches tall
A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall

questions.correctAnswerText: A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall
questions.explanation: Children who are eight or older and at least 4 feet 9 inches tall can use a regular safety belt. All other children must use a child passenger restraint system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the road?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a car's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibration to alert sleepy drivers that they left the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibration to alert sleepy drivers that they left the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn tired or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt before you drive. Never adjust mirrors while your vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay within your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should a driver watch?

options.text: Only straight ahead.
Only the middle of the road.
Beside, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beside, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your vehicle to be a safe driver.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as normal traffic fines.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones to protect drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your car?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What rule helps prevent tailgating?

options.text: The one-second rule.
The two-second rule.
The three-second rule.

questions.correctAnswerText: The three-second rule.
questions.explanation: Use the three-second rule. When the car ahead passes a point, count to three. If you reach that point before you finish counting, you are following too closely.

questions.question: What should you do when a blind person with a guide dog or white cane crosses?

options.text: Always yield the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross.
Only yield at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast someone absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex and how much food is in their stomach. The only way to remove alcohol is to wait.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when there is a deep puddle ahead?

options.text: Drive through at the posted speed.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid puddles and other slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. A dry, solid surface is safest for driving.

questions.question: Where can you legally keep an opened alcoholic beverage in your car?

options.text: Under the front seat.
In the glove compartment.
In the trunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the trunk.
questions.explanation: An opened alcoholic beverage must be in the trunk, away from passengers. The glove compartment is not allowed.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto the freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near traffic speed, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: What should you never do when changing lanes?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Always use your turn signal to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Adjust your speed to avoid accidents and brake damage.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass until after the sign.
Do not pass unless it seems safe.
Do not pass for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass for any reason.
questions.explanation: White rectangular signs show rules you must obey. This sign means never pass other vehicles in this area.

questions.question: When parking in an unusual area, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Make sure your parked car is visible to drivers from any direction so it does not become a hazard.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with hazardous load signs?

options.text: They cannot drive on freeways.
They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
They cannot go faster than 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: After a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for another train and wait until all gates are raised and all warning lights have stopped before crossing.
